The gate below therefore uses the noise each batch measures for itself.

items.title: Fix the eager-path doorbell payload so the in-engine profiler works
items.status: done 2026-10-21: the profiler works on this CUDA build (31 of 31 requests printed a stage table, 0 payload errors); the failure was A770/SYCL-only (docs/WINDOW_PROFILE_CUDA.md)
items.detail: STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE and STRATA_VERIFY_EAGER both fail with 'verify: layer 0 rang but its payload never arrived whole', reproducibly 3/3. Likely defect: the eager path does not publish the doorbell payload doorbell_payload_ready waits for, so the host spins to the 2 s timeout. Debug-only path; normal graph-mode inference is unaffected.
items.caveat: recorded on the A770/SYCL build. Confirm it reproduces on this CUDA build before treating it as the same bug.
items.done_when: either the profiler produces per-stage timings on this CUDA build, or the failure is confirmed A770-only and item 3 proceeds on item 2's numbers alone

items.title: Measure the doorbell round-trip latency (ring -> host -> flag -> GPU) and how much of the window is idle GPU time
items.status: done 2026-10-21: doorbell round trip (waitA) 0.32 ms/window, 0.5% of a 59.4 ms window; the GPU waits 65.4% of the window, 59.2% of it on the PCIe-share copies (waitB) and 6.0% on the CPU pool (docs/WINDOW_PROFILE_CUDA.md, tools/read_window_profile.py)
items.source: docs/A770_SPEED_SPEC.md, end of 'GPU utilization: the GPU is mostly IDLE during decode'
items.done_when: a measured round-trip latency in ms and a measured idle-GPU fraction on this machine, from interleaved runs with state capture, against the 24.3% floor

items.title: Cut the GPU's wait for the PCIe share of the missed experts (waitB)
items.status: gate MET 2026-10-22 (the re-run this item asked for): the automatic share against --pcie-frac 0.35 alone, 5 rounds x 2 runs, agent test, profiler on (bench/results/ab-pcie-frac-rerun). waitB's share of the window falls, no overlap between the arms: baseline 61.2/59.9/59.2/61.9/59.7, arm 55.4/55.5/56.2/54.1/56.2 (tools/read_window_profile.py, per-launch engine-log.txt). Decode: the tool of record (tools/summarize_ab_sweep.py) pairs each arm launch with the baseline at the same turn, +6.7/+2.9/+4.5/+10.4/+6.0, median +6.0%, above the batch's own floor (2.3% over the warm baseline launches); sign holds 5 of 5 in both readers. Dissent recorded: tools/read_sweep_warm.py says its per-turn distributions overlap (biggest arm gap 12.7% vs its own noise row 5.6%). The arm logs print no share line (an explicit flag switches the refinement off) so that check is 0.45-vs-0.35 and the arm's half is read through PCIe experts/layer-window 3.18-3.67 -> 2.48-2.62 (ratio 0.72 vs the 0.78 predicted). Next: (b) split waitB into copy time and source time. Sub-step (b) done 2026-10-22 (bench/results/ab-tier-split-rerun, tools/tier_split_rerun.bat, same sweep/arms/5 rounds): the mechanism test FAILS - the arm's file-tier blob count is lower in 2 of 5 round-pairs (2.50 and 2.00 against a baseline whose five medians are all 3.00, spread zero), not the 4 of 5 the rule asked for, and the RAM tier moved no consistent way. The share check passes (baseline 16.2/16.4/16.3/16.4/15.8 pct, arm 11.5/13.1/12.0/11.8/11.9, ratio 0.74 vs 0.78) and waitB's share still falls 5/5 with no overlap (61.2/61.6/59.1/61.0/59.3 -> 54.7/57.0/56.3/56.7/55.7), reproducing the batch above. So the gate was met, but the saving did not come from the bus share: the source side is the file tier's ~2.2 ms/window (unchanged between arms) plus a RAM tier whose clock, on for the first time (STRATA_RAM_TIER_CLOCK=1), reads 0.00 ms/window - under 6% of a 33-41 ms waitB, and the part that did not move. Speed on this batch: tool of record median +2.2% inside its own 3.2% floor, sign 5/5; read_sweep_warm cannot separate (floor 3.7%, largest gap 5.2%, distributions overlap). (c): the data points at the copy itself, not the source - and STRATA_DMA_BATCH (docs/BATCHED_DMA.md) is already built for exactly that and has never been run as a proper batch. Full write-up: docs/WINDOW_PROFILE_CUDA.md. Earlier, 2026-10-21: --pcie-frac 0.25/0.35/0.45/0.60 against the automatic share - 0.60 is worse (-7.6%), 0.25 and 0.45 equal automatic, 0.35 is +7.2% per turn but not separated from that batch's own noise (docs/WINDOW_PROFILE_CUDA.md)
items.detail: Per window (59.4 ms median, 31 requests): waitB 35.5 ms, waitCPU 3.1 ms, doorbell waitA 0.32 ms; 3.25 PCIe experts per layer-window. At the probed 27.2 GB/s the copies should take at most ~15 ms per window, so part of waitB is not the link - the file tier, late copies, or an early wait are the candidates, none measured. Steps: (a) --pcie-frac arms against the automatic 0.55 (0.40, 0.25: work moves from the copies to the CPU pool, whose wait is small), interleaved, each launch run with STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1 STRATA_DECODE_TIMING=1 so read_window_profile.py gives waitB per arm; (b) split waitB into copy time and source time (file tier versus the page-locked RAM tier); (c) only then a code change to the copy path, if (a)-(b) point at one.
items.caveat: the profiler's stamps add their own time, so read the shares, not the absolute milliseconds, and compare arms measured the same way
items.done_when: waitB's share of the window falls and decode rises by more than the noise the batch measures for itself, under the interleaved control - or the bus-share arms are stated as not moving it, which closes the lever

items.title: Write up the adapt-kv sweep honestly: nothing separated
items.status: done 2026-10-21 (b63be2eb): both write-ups carry the same verdict, nothing separated; every number reproduces through tools/read_sweep_warm.py
items.detail: 13 arms, three runs each, all within their own noise. The biggest arm gap (72.6%, adapt-swaps 16) sits inside the noise row's own per-turn range (54-98%), so the data cannot separate them and the honest verdict is 'nothing separated', not a story about which arm won. Cache-off is the contrast: its arm (28-44%) lies wholly outside its repeats (1-24%).
items.done_when: docs/SWEEP_ADAPT_KV.md and bench/results/ab-adapt-kv-sweep/SWEEP_ADAPT_KV.md tell the same story, and every number in both reproduces through tools/summarize_ab_sweep.py or tools/read_sweep_warm.py

no gain: --kv k8v4, --prefill auto:16384, a smaller VRAM reserve, --adapt-async

open_knobs.note: real lever, automatic (it picks 0.55 on this link's 27.2 GB/s probe); item 3 now sets it on purpose, because items 1-2 put 59% of the window in the wait for the PCIe share
real lever, already measured as a wash on the A770; do not re-open as a sizing question
real lever, its own experiment with its own parity gate, never a side effect of a memory sweep

deferred_tuning.gate: an arm must clear the noise its own batch measures - the repeated-baseline rows, computed by tools/summarize_ab_sweep.py or tools/read_sweep_warm.py, never asserted - under the interleaved control; 24.3% (BENCH_NOISE.md, before 2026-10-18) is the historical figure, not a fixed bar

execution.mode: end-to-end by Claude, no per-package review
execution.my_role: recommendations are binding as recommendations - take them, but a gate that fails stops the item and gets reported, not worked around
rules: one change per commit, message says what was measured, not what was hoped
every number written into a doc must reproduce off disk with the tool of record named in the doc
the verdict line in any tool must be computed, never asserted
numbers already in the docs are correct as written - do not re-derive them from rounded medians
run tools/test_strata_ab.py before committing; it must stay at 31 passing
